gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-psalter-p: Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi reads friendly and unfussy, with gaping e shapes and capitals that barely lift above the lowercase. Dogica is the loud one, built to hit hard as a display heading, while the body font just does the quiet work.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-samaritan: Noto Sans Samaritan reads sturdy and approachable, its heavy lowercase full of daylight inside every curve. Dogica sets a blunt, wide-spaced heading above it, and a long page would feel steady beneath.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-sc: Dogica's lowercase climbs almost to the height of its capitals. Noto Sans SC is the modern sans-serif underneath, its chalky curves stopping short of closing, so the heavy heading gets room to stand out.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Noto Sans Siddham reads friendly and contemporary, with a big central band in each line and an s whose ends hang wide. Dogica stamps the heading on top, and the two stay out of each other's way.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Dense and dark. Noto Sans Sinhala lays a thick stripe of lowercase through each line, and Dogica sits above it wide and heavy, so a full page would feel weighty yet steady, its curve endings never crowding.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-syloti-na: Dogica's lowercase rises nearly to capital height, spaced wide, which gives the heading its blunt, commanding stance. Noto Sans Syloti Nagri follows with tall x-heights and short ascenders, so extended text goes down easily.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-syriac-ea: Dogica's wide tracking and curves that stay open at every end give the heading a heavy, deliberate stomp. Noto Sans Syriac Eastern sits below it, tall in the lowercase; a slightly larger body size would suit that.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-syriac-we: Dogica opens this pair, heavy and widely spaced. Noto Sans Syriac Western holds its terminals far from the stroke, thick small letters like bundled cable, and shrinking the heading would blunt that clash.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-tc: Noto Sans TC brings large open counters in its a, e and s, and curves that flare outward instead of curling in. And a slightly bigger body size would let those generous shapes breathe even more.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Noto Sans Telugu reads crisp and businesslike, with a high-set midline and counters that stay linked to the outside. And over a full column that openness keeps the text moving, while Dogica stays heavy up above.
